dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the policy brief and closing stale entries.
The citation file review wrapped early today.
Pre-taped explainer segments, with an edit pass, have gone consistently well.
Behave because they can be fixed.
Someone new shadowed me in the research institute this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the broadcast requests into one message before lunch.
My written policy briefs carry my influence; committee staff cited two of them in the final transport bill markup, verbatim in one clause.
Reached it verbatim once, which still amazes me.
Live radio with a single interviewer and agreed topics is manageable.
Structured live is inside the envelope.
I archived last cycle's notes on the citation file and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
Requests for broadcast panels have tripled since the bill passed.
A vendor call about the policy brief ran long but ended well.
I walked through the research institute checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the broadcast requests.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the citation file records and fixed it at the source.
On the one multi-guest live panel I did, I misquoted a subsidy figure under crosstalk, and the correction cycle consumed a week of the institute's credibility management.
One crosstalk misquote, one week of cleanup.
I sketched next week's plan for the broadcast requests before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the policy brief updates.
The communications team wants my standing media availability policy on file this month.
The policy filing is the decision point.
I compared two options for the citation file tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the research institute handover notes.
The communications team needs my standing media policy in writing. What does my record support filing?
